hook: Andreessen co-created the Mosaic web browser while working at the University of Illinois's National Center for Supercomputing Applications, then co-founded Netscape. Since 2009 he has run the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz with Ben Horowitz, which names AI among its core investment areas. He has also written some of the most widely circulated arguments for building AI quickly, including Why AI Will Save the World in 2023.

timeline.event: Mosaic, the browser he co-created at NCSA with Eric Bina, is released
timeline.impact: Helps popularise graphical browsing of the web.

timeline.event: Leaves NCSA and co-founds with Jim Clark the company that becomes Netscape Communications
timeline.impact: Launches Netscape Navigator, a commercial web browser.

timeline.event: Joins the boards of Facebook in June and of Hewlett-Packard
timeline.impact: Begins a board role that continues at Meta Platforms.

timeline.event: Andreessen Horowitz is announced on July 6, co-founded with Ben Horowitz
timeline.impact: Establishes the venture firm he still leads.

timeline.event: Publishes Why Software Is Eating the World in The Wall Street Journal on August 20
timeline.impact: Sets out a widely cited argument about software's spread across industries.

timeline.event: Receives the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering
timeline.impact: Shares the inaugural prize with four other pioneers of the internet and the web.

timeline.event: Publishes Why AI Will Save the World on June 6 and The Techno-Optimist Manifesto on October 16
timeline.impact: Argues that fears about AI are overstated and that the technology should be built quickly.

timeline.impact: Takes an advisory role on federal science and technology policy.

quick_facts: Holds a bachelor's degree in computer science from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
Co-created the Mosaic browser at the university's National Center for Supercomputing Applications, released in 1993.
Co-founder and general partner of Andreessen Horowitz, which he started with Ben Horowitz in 2009.
Has served on the board of Meta Platforms, formerly Facebook, since June 2008, and served on the board of Hewlett-Packard from 2008 to 2018.
Shared the 2013 Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering with Louis Pouzin, Robert Kahn, Vinton Cerf and Tim Berners-Lee for the internet and the web.
Was named in March 2026 to the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.

achievements.title: Mosaic and Netscape
achievements.impact: Mosaic helped bring graphical web browsing to a general audience, and Netscape, which he co-founded with Jim Clark in 1994, turned that work into a commercial browser before AOL bought the company in 1999.

achievements.title: Co-founder, Andreessen Horowitz
achievements.impact: The firm he founded with Ben Horowitz in 2009 reports more than $100 billion under management across its funds as of April 2026 and lists AI among its main investment areas.

achievements.title: Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering, 2013
achievements.impact: One of five inaugural winners recognised for the creation of the internet and the web, cited for co-authoring Mosaic.

achievements.title: Essays on software and AI
achievements.impact: Why Software Is Eating the World (2011), Why AI Will Save the World (2023) and The Techno-Optimist Manifesto (2023) set out his case that software and AI should be built and deployed aggressively.

achievements.title: Board member, Meta Platforms
achievements.impact: Has served on the company's board since June 2008 and sits on its Risk and Strategy Committee.

source_basis: This profile was written mainly from the Wikipedia article on Marc Andreessen, retrieved 2026-10-22, with awards, dates and current role checked against Andreessen Horowitz's about and author pages, Meta's board listing, the Queen Elizabeth Prize site and the White House PCAST announcement.
